rationale: Ground truth is essentially empty (bot rate-limit messages and 'thanks'), so recall is vacuous for both. Both candidates independently found the same central, well-verified defect (new test file lacks pytestmark, so CI's marker-filtered selector silently deselects it) and converge on several secondary nits (stale Blackwell docs language, pyproject.toml comment, sm_110a narrative inconsistency, misleading env-override docs). X edges ahead by surfacing two additional, higher-severity, well-grounded correctness bugs Y missed entirely: warmup_quack_fp8() bypassing the capability gate (a real crash/slowdown risk on the exact hardware this PR protects) and a sharp catch that vLLM's warning_once keys on the exception object so it never actually dedupes. Y's unique findings (10.x/11.x gate-scope ambiguity, doc enumeration nitpick) are valid but lower-impact and one is arguably redundant since the doc already states 'compute capability 10.x'. Both are highly actionable with concrete file:line fixes; Y's literal ```suggestion``` blocks are marginally more mechanical, but X's clearer severity triage and deeper unique catches make it the stronger review overall.
